messages.subject: Finding tags in specific folder
parts:
I just started learning camtrapR, and having some naïve issues. I will be grateful if someone can help. I tagged photos in digiKam, but I can't see those tags in the folder where I am storing the camera trap photos. Which settings do I need to change to see those? 

Thank you, 
Hasan

messages.author: fad1b5962e30b073
messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Finding tags in specific folder
parts:
you don't need to manually tag them. Set a digikam database for the folder structure you created to keep the images. it will take a while for the database 5o read them out.

And, why digikam? do you have videos? otherwise, you can just do fine with exiftool.

cheers.

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Finding tags in specific folder
parts:
Hi, 
when you say "I can't see those tags in the folder where I am storing the camera trap photos", do you mean in Windows Explorer? That is normal. I think Explorer only shows XMP:Keywords, but the digiKam tags are written in the HierarchicalSubject metadata slot. That may be a little inconvenient, but should be no problem.
What is more important is that the tags are saved in the metadata of the image. You can check that with exifTagNames(). Search for the "HierarchicalSubject" tag group and see if the values contain the tags you assigned in digiKam. 
If the tags are there, you can run recordTable() and other functions which read out the metadata tags assigned in digiKam

Regarding the second comment, there may be a misunderstanding regarding using metadata tags for species ID (which currently requires digiKam) vs. using species directories. When using species directories, you don't need digiKam (but there are also some drawbacks, see vignette 2). If you use metadata tags, you need digiKam (or possibly Adobe Bridge).
Exiftool and digiKam serve very different purposes. digiKam is most useful for tagging images with a nice user interface and lots of powerful image management options. Exiftool is a command line tool that can read image metadata and the tags assigned in digiKam, and R can then use the output of Exiftool for making record tables etc. So it's really two very different pieces of software, and Exiftool can't do the tagging for you. 

If this doesn't answer your question please let us know or share some screenshots.
Best regards,
Jürgen
